items.title: Scott Yanow interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 22, 2021
items.q: You know you have Benny Goodman and Duke Ellington... I think if someone comes up with a completely new way of playing jazz, like Charlie Parker or someone who has just so many innovations in their career like Duke Ellington, you’d call them geniuses.

ctx.x: It’s so interesting you say that because I shouldn’t talk about myself but very briefly I went out to get my first John Coltrane record because someone said, “You should listen to him.” And I picked up “Om.” And that was not a great place to start for me, and I’m afraid it scared me off for quite a while.

But you know it’s just the basic idea I liked to hear how it all evolved and how it all connects together. And because I was lucky enough to start with Dixieland and the 1920s jazz, I still love listening to that today, where most critics and jazz journalists, they don’t go further back from Charlie Parker, usually. You know you have Benny Goodman and Duke Ellington, but they’re not really going to go back to the earliest music because the recording quality doesn’t agree with them and it seems too simple. They…
Do you feel that there’s a determination on their part that that music wasn’t really an art form or worthy of being an art form, thus worthy of critiquing?
